task_spec: SUBJECT: tier what a reconstruct run counts as a metadata conflict - the three MEASURED attributes (filesize, playtime_float, bitrate) stop raising a conflict and follow the winning record through the entry_patches path they already travel, the three EDITORIAL attributes (artist, title, album) raise one exactly as today, and the run's report names how many groups the rule settled and lists every group whose measured-attribute gap exceeds a relative band as an outlier READING rather than a row to decide.

scope: traktor_nml/splice.py (the divergence rule at :341 and what a ConflictRow carries), traktor_nml/reconstruct_report.py and the CLI reconstruct command (the settled count and the outlier listing), traktor_nml/gui/conflict_model.py, the Resolve and Preview surfaces in traktor_nml/gui/app.py, design/reconnect-wizard/*.dc.html where the screen changes, tests/, docs/

rejected_alternatives: a relative band as THE rule (user's first choice, withdrawn on measurement) - group-level survivors are 2,203 rows at 1% and the curve plateaus past it, so ~1,650 measured divergences sit above any band; the band survives only as the outlier threshold
technical attributes never conflict with no outlier listing ('tier, plain') - rejected because the 6 playtime_float groups beyond 1%, worst 3,516s, would pass unnamed
keeping playtime_float conflicting while tiering filesize and bitrate - rejected: the user took the outlier listing INSTEAD of that

redrawing the Resolve table bulk-first or paginated as the fix for the freeze - the rule removes 94.2% of rows, so the freeze is expected to go with them; any bound is defence in depth, to be decided explicitly
widening reconnect_timeout as the fix - moves the threshold without addressing what holds the loop
current_understanding: splice.py:341 compares raw attribute strings by set size, so '8123' vs '8124' KB is a divergence and becomes a conflict group the operator must decide.

Measured on the user's real collection pair (9,052 groups, two inputs): 8,113 groups (89.6%) diverge on filesize ALONE; 8,523 (94.2%) on nothing but the three measured attributes; 529 (5.8%) touch artist/title/album.

filesize: 7,469 groups diverge, gap min 1 KB, median 2 KB, max 16,425,110 KB, relative median 0.0162%, max 99.9%. playtime_float: 70 groups, median 0.0392s, max 3,516.5s. bitrate: 402 groups, median 89, max 1,091,200.
Group-level band survivors: 0.01% -> 7,279; 0.1% -> 2,679; 1% -> 2,203; 5% -> 2,180; 10% -> 2,176. The plateau past 1% is why a band cannot be the rule.

The widest measured gaps are one file described twice: .stem.m4a filesize at roughly a 4x ratio (17564 vs 69203) and .aif bitrate 1411000 vs 320000 - two Traktor analyses disagreeing about what to measure in a container, on the same LOCATION.

BUG this removes as a side effect: draw() (app.py:2661) builds all 9,052 rows on the event loop, measured at 8.5-10.1s; nicegui's budget is 6s (ping_interval 4s + ping_timeout 2s, nicegui.py:138-139, from the default reconnect_timeout 3.0 that __main__.py:19 does not override); the socket drops, client.py:383-388 deletes the client after 3s, and because wizard state lives in the @ui.page builder's closures the reconnect can only rebuild - the run is lost and the window returns to step 1. Reproduction: load the user's two collections on /, click Preview. 529 rows at the measured 0.64ms/row is under a second.
assumptions: The measured-attribute tier does not change which record wins a group, only whether the group is put to the operator (H - entry_patches substitutes the named record's values either way; must be verified against the resolution path)
Some recorded baseline or golden output carries conflict rows whose counts change under the new rule (M-H - the parity question below; must be found before implementation, not during)

The outlier band and the tier can share one nicegui-free module that both the CLI report and conflict_model read, so the screen and the printed run cannot disagree (M - structure to be decided in planning)

A group that diverges on both an editorial and a measured attribute stays a conflict on the editorial attribute alone, and its measured divergence is not listed twice (M - the plan must state what such a group's attrs tuple holds and whether it can also be an outlier)
reconstruct_report.py is where an outlier listing belongs rather than splice.py (M - splice reports rows; the report composes sentences)
invisible_knowledge: A conflict compares Traktor against Traktor, so a measured difference is a real recorded fact. The reason to tier is NOT that the difference is unreal - it is that no operator judgement exists for a measured attribute. That is the opposite of matching.py's reason for tolerating one (Traktor against the disk, two measurement systems), which is why the two rules must not be described as the same idea or share a tolerance.
entry_patches already substitutes _TRACKED_ATTRS values from the named record, so a tiered attribute still travels with the winner: the written file does not silently keep base's number.

The one user-visible exposure is playtime_float - 6 groups beyond 1%, worst 3,516s, which shows as a wrong track length in Traktor until it re-analyses. The outlier listing is what the user accepted INSTEAD of keeping playtime conflicting, so it must actually name those groups, not merely count them.

A WAV converted to .stem.m4a changes the filename, so it changes the primary key and is never a conflict at all - it is a dangling entry for the reconnect wizard. The new rule must not be documented as covering that case.

Tiering is a change to what the operator is asked, not to what the tool records: the count of groups settled by the rule is read off the model (DL-215) so the screen and the CLI cannot disagree about how many decisions were made for the operator.

9,052 rows was never a screen anyone could work; the volume was the symptom, and both collections settle every group by either bulk action, so the per-row table earns its place only for rows a rule cannot reach.
